summary: A full-screen map of resting order-book liquidity over time, with trade bubbles, a price ladder on the right and volume bars below.
overview: Liquidity Map turns the chart into a view of the order book. The size resting at each price shows as a glow, from deep blue for small size to yellow, orange and red for the biggest walls.
A thin price line runs through it, with bubbles for traded volume, an order-book ladder on the right and volume bars along the bottom.
how: For crypto it reads the exchange's public order book and trade stream, plus recorded book history. Each time bucket becomes one column of the heatmap. A wall that is pulled or filled simply stops.

Trade bubbles are sized by traded volume and split green and red by the share of aggressive buying and selling. The right-hand columns show the current size per price and the running total from the best price outward.
use: Use it to see where size is resting and whether price trades into it or away from it.
Some traders watch bubbles that appear right at a bright wall.
Use the ladder to read the size near the current price at a glance.
Turn Hide candles off if you want to keep your candles under the map.
notes: It describes resting orders and prints. It does not predict anything and has no order buttons.
Futures depth for this tool is limited to admins for now; crypto works for Pro members.
Contrast and size filters change only how the map looks, not the data.
